SPEC COMPLIANCE CHUNK CQL-15: CQL — Interval Operators Part 1. Test these items: After precision (Interval), Before precision (Interval), Collapse(argument, [per]), Contains precision (Interval, point), End of (Interval), Ends precision, Equal (Interval), Equivalent (Interval), Except (Interval), Expand(argument, [per]), In precision (point, Interval), Includes precision (Interval). For DuckDB-backed FHIRPath/CQL surfaces, test both the native/C++ extension path and the Python fallback where both exist, and compare outputs between paths. For SQL-on-FHIR ViewDefinition chunks, test parser validation, SQL generation, DuckDB execution, and official spec fixtures/examples relevant to the chunk.

When the pipeline is fully complete, set workflow to null, set exit_reason, write all handoff files, and return control to the outer spec compliance orchestrator.

issues.evidence: Interval[@2012-01-01,@2012-01-15] ends day of Interval[@2012-01-05,@2012-01-15] -> true; spec/reference EndsEvaluator: start(A)>=start(B) AND end(A)==end(B) at precision -> false. Point-precision variant Interval[@2024-01-01,@2024-01-05] ends day of @2024-01-05 also true (should be false; degenerate-interval promotion, consistent with no-precision path intervalEndsSame). Root: _translate_ends_op 'precision of' branch compares intervalEnd equality only. Repro: .temp/qa/cql15_skeptic/probe2.py EndsPrecSpec. Both engines.
issues.root_cause: _translate_ends_op 'precision of' branch compared intervalEnd equality only; dropped start(A)>=start(B) conjunct of CQL §9 Ends
issues.resolution: ends <prec> now emits start(left)>=start(right) AND end(left)==end(right) at precision; point right promotes to degenerate-interval semantics

issues.evidence: collapse {Interval[1,3],Interval[5,6]} per 2 -> {[1,2],[5,6]} (truncates input bounds!); reference: per extends each interval's end by per for the merge decision -> {[1,6]}; per 1 fails to merge; Decimal per explodes {[1,3],[3.5,6]} per 1.0 into 6 singletons; output intervals must preserve original bounds. Root cause: translator lowers collapse(X,per) as collapse_intervals(expand(X,per)) (_functions.py _translate_collapse). Existing test pins (test_interval_part1_parity CollapseValidPer) encode the wrong behavior. Both engines.
issues.root_cause: _translate_collapse lowered collapse(X,per) as collapse_intervals(expand(X,per)), reusing expand grid semantics instead of per-extended merge windows
issues.resolution: collapse(X,per) lowers to new collapse_intervals_per UDF (Python udf/interval.py + native CollapseIntervalsPerFunc, md5-verified deploy 025c79ed...); per extends each interval's end for the merge decision only; output keeps original bounds; temporal per of 1/0 uses precision meets

issues.spec_citation: CQL 1.5 §9 Collapse per; reference: per value 0 -> intervals unchanged
issues.evidence: collapse {Interval[1,3],Interval[4,6]} per 0: Python path returns inverted intervals [1,0],[4,3] (invalid); native path returns []. Reference: merge via meets -> {[1,6]}. Same root cause as QA-002 (expand-wrap with 0 step).
issues.root_cause: expand-wrap with per value 0: Python emitted inverted intervals, native emitted [] — no shared merge semantics
issues.resolution: covered by QA-002 fix; per 0 → no extension → meets merge

issues.evidence: { Interval[1,5], Interval[10,12] } except Interval[2,3] -> BinderException 'array_length(VARCHAR)': CQLListExceptEq receives scalar intervalFromBounds VARCHAR as right arg; macro expects LIST. Valid CQL must coerce interval to singleton list. Both engines. Repro: probe2.py ExceptListArg.
issues.root_cause: list-except branch passed scalar intervalFromBounds VARCHAR into CQLListExceptEq(list,...) macro
issues.resolution: literal Interval operands coerced via list_value() before CQLListExceptEq; identifiers untouched
